title: Pin rollback impact matrix and operator playbook
content:
Purpose
---
This doc is a working operator playbook for performing region-pin rollbacks and assessing customer impact. Focus: minimize data residency violations while restoring service quickly. Not final — notes, queries, and comm templates included.

Context and why this exists
- We pin tenants to regions to meet compliance (region pin).
- Rollbacks are needed when a pin change causes outages, mis-routing, or unacceptable latency.
- Rollback must avoid creating evidence of cross-border access that breaks customer commitments.

Quick summary of rollback decision flow (short)
1) Detect: telemetry alert or customer report (latency SLO breaches, 5xx routing errors).
2) Triage: confirm root cause is recent pin change/propagation.
3) Assess exposure: which tenants, which data types, how long since pin change?
4) Rollback plan: choose immediate revert or staged revert with fallbacks.
5) Execute with audit capture: ensure logs show operator action and timeline.
6) Customer comms and follow-up: update customers and schedule postmortem.

Operator-runbook steps (detailed)
- Preconditions (must verify before rolling back):
  - Confirm operator has active session MFA and escalation approval (if > 10 tenants affected).
  - Confirm backup control-plane snapshot exists for the customers in question (timestamped).
  - Ensure network egress rules/certs in target region are not modified during revert.

- Detection signals to correlate:
  - route-5xx-rate > baseline (operator dashboards)
  - token-latency-percentile spike (p95 > configured SLO)
  - telemetry: location-mismatch events (request region != tenant pinned region)
  - customer support tickets mentioning region or latency keywords

- Immediate triage checklist (10 minute window):
  1) Identify commit id and deploy window for pin change (console -> rollouts -> audit).
  2) Query: "SELECT tenant_id, pin_change_ts, previous_region FROM residency_changes WHERE pin_change_ts >= :window"; filter by affected IDs.
  3) Cross-check KV cache warmup status and any prefix-cache misses.
  4) Confirm routing table snapshots and edge-proxy versions.

- Impact matrix (how to decide safe revert vs staged)
  Rows: Tenant criticality | Data locality sensitivity | Sessions open | Estimated cross-border exposure | Recommended action
  - High | High | Many | >30min | Immediate revert + notify legal and customer
  - High | Medium | Some | <30min | Staged revert with canary-targeting and audit
  - Medium | Low | Few | N/A | Wait for graceful draining and scheduled revert
  - Low | Low | None | None | Defer to batch maintenance window

Notes on evidence-sensitive rollback constraints
- If revert would cause reads to occur in the old region (i.e., pulling state from non-authoritative storage), consider performing a read-only redirect or proxy that still guarantees data anchors remain in pinned region.
- Never perform a rollback that triggers a cross-border replication job; if replication will run as part of revert, pause replication and coordinate with legal/compliance.
- Capture operator audit logs: who, when, what keys, affected tenant list. Tag these logs with a legal artifact id.

Rollback execution - CLI and console ops (examples)
- Console (preferred for minor rollbacks):
  1) Console -> Residency -> Tenant -> Revert pin -> select snapshot -> apply with dry-run flag ON -> monitor metrics for 2 min -> confirm apply.
- CLI (for bulk):
  - dry-run: residencyctl revert --tenant-file tenants.csv --snapshot 2025-11-05T14:00Z --dry-run
  - execute: residencyctl revert --tenant-file tenants.csv --snapshot 2025-11-05T14:00Z --execute --audit-id ROLLBACK-<YYYYMMDD>-<operator>

Telemetry queries to run immediately after revert (examples)
- p95-latency-by-tenant (last 15m)
- cross-border-access-events count (last 24h)
- routing-error-rate by edge-proxy (last 30m)
- kv-cache-hit-rate by tenant and region (last 15m)
- Example Influx/PromQL: sum(rate(requests_total{tenant=~"$TENANT"} [1m])) by (region, code)

Customer communication templates (short)
- Immediate ack (Support -> Customer): "We’re investigating elevated latency and routing errors affecting your account. We’ve identified a recent region configuration change as a potential cause and are preparing a controlled rollback. We’ll provide ETA within 30 minutes and will not make any changes that could expand cross-border processing without your consent."
- Post-rollback update: "We reverted the region configuration at <time>. Service metrics indicate latency/error rates returned to baseline. No cross-border access was observed (audit id: ROLLBACK-20260310-AISHA). Follow-up: technical postmortem scheduled."

Legal/compliance escalation guidance
- If estimated cross-border exposure > 15 minutes for sensitive tenants, immediately notify Compliance with: tenant list, time window, steps taken, and evidence bundle id. Use channel #compliance-residency and file a compliance incident per SOP-RES-01.
- For customers with contractual territory clauses, attach signed contract excerpt to the incident.

Post-rollback follow-up actions
- 24-hour monitoring: keep telemetry retention of p95/p99 for affected tenants and mark dashboards.
- Postmortem: run a mini-PM with SRE + Product + Legal + Sales for affected tenants within 72 hours.
- Remediation tasks: root cause (deployment orchestration bug?), confirm region pin gating in CI, add unit/regression tests around pin roll.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Do we have an automated preflight that simulates the pin change for each tenant's geo-evidence rules? If not, add a ticket.
- Need a small agent that can do a dry-run revert and assert no replication jobs will start; file JIRA-RESID-889 to implement.
- Clarify SLA on operator notification thresholds for >5 tenants affected.

Appendix: sample incident timeline template (fill during incident)
- 00:00 Alert -> alert-id -> owner
- 00:03 Triage summary: suspected cause
- 00:10 Decision: rollback immediate / staged / none
- 00:15 Action: revert executed (audit id)
- 00:20 Monitor: p95/p99 baseline comparison
- 00:40 Customer update sent
- 24:00 Post-rollback check-in

Short glossary
- Pin: tenant-to-region mapping used for routing and storage anchor decisions.
- Revert: operation that restores previous pin snapshot.
- Cross-border exposure: any read/write that occurs outside tenant's contractual region during the incident window.

References / related docs
- CONFLUENCE-1234 (residency architecture)
- JIRA-RESID-889 (rollback automation backlog)

-- end of working draft --
